title: Tokaji
subtitle: Aszú, Szamorodni and Eszencia
objectives: Explain how Aszú is made in detail

steps.title: Aszú
steps.body: Aszú berries, shrivelled by botrytis, are picked one by one and stored as a paste. They're added to a base wine or fermenting must, soaked for 12 to 60 hours, then pressed. Traditionally, sweetness was measured in puttonyos, the number of 25 kg baskets of aszú per 136-litre barrel. Since 2013, Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar.

steps.title: Szamorodni and Eszencia
steps.body: Szamorodni, meaning as it comes, is made from whole bunches with some aszú berries, not separated. It can be dry, aged under a flor-like yeast, or sweet. Eszencia is the free-run juice that drips from aszú berries under their own weight. It can have over 450 g/l of sugar, ferments for years, and rarely reaches 5% alcohol.

steps.prompt: Match each Tokaji to its making.
steps.explanation: Tokaj makes several wines from the same harvest.

steps.title: Ageing
steps.body: Tokaji Aszú ages at least 18 months in oak, traditionally small Gönci barrels of 136 litres, in cellars cut into volcanic rock, lined with a black mould, Zasmidium cellare, that regulates humidity. High acidity from Furmint lets these wines age for a century or more.

steps.prompt: Tokaji ____ is the free-run juice from aszú berries.
steps.explanation: Eszencia is so sweet it ferments very slowly and stays very low in alcohol.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aszú berries are soaked in base wine, giving at least 120 g/l of sugar
Szamorodni uses whole bunches; Eszencia is pure free-run juice
Furmint's acidity lets Tokaji age for a century
